port.name: Herdr
port.description: Living Code for Herdr: complete native theme overrides for the sidebar, panels, selections, status indicators and workspace chrome.

guide.installation:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/living-code-theme/herdr.git
cd herdr
```

Open the desired `themes/living-code-*.toml` file and merge its `[theme]` and `[theme.custom]` sections into your Herdr config, normally `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`. Replace existing theme sections rather than appending duplicate TOML tables; keep your workspaces, keybindings and integrations. `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` overrides this location.

Restart Herdr or reload the running server config:

```sh
herdr server reload-config
```
guide.configuration: Every documented custom token is supplied. `auto_switch = false` makes the chosen flavor deterministic; Paper uses a light built-in fallback, all other flavors use a dark fallback. For appearance switching, Herdr also accepts `[theme.custom.light]` and `[theme.custom.dark]`; combine the selected light/dark overrides intentionally rather than duplicating `[theme]` tables.
guide.compatibility: The custom-token interface is present in Herdr 0.9.3 and is checked against the pinned upstream Rust fields. This themes Herdr’s own UI. Embedded terminal panes inherit the host terminal’s palette and application-specific themes, so install the matching Living Code terminal theme too. No agent sessions or workspaces are created by this port.
